title: 'Go get a job, don't rob from us': Harlingen RV park residents respond after break-ins - NewsBreak
text:
By Jorge Vela ,
50 minutes ago HARLINGEN, Texas ( ValleyCentral ) — A series of burglaries at a Harlingen RV park has left residents concerned and prompted neighbors to take extra steps to protect their community.
According to the Harlingen Police Department, officers have received about half a dozen reports of break-ins at Encore Paradise Park over the past several weeks.
Police say many of the victims are Winter Texans who have returned to their home states for the summer, leaving some RVs and mobile homes unoccupied and vulnerable to theft.
Investigators said most of the burglaries involved items stolen from storage sheds, although some mobile homes were also targeted.
“It’s not too good seeing how this is supposed to be a secure park,” resident Blake Klwalski said.
Authorities are reviewing tips and a photograph of a person of interest that has been circulating on social media. Police believe the suspect may be entering the park through a weak section of a chain-link fence.
Residents say the suspect has repeatedly cut through the fencing, leaving neighbors responsible for repair costs.
“They don’t even go over, they just take the bolt cutters and go right through it, and then we have to call the guy to come fix that and pay for that,” Klwalski said. “The guy comes out the next day, but they just come back with bolt cutters.”
Klwalski said residents have become increasingly worried after reports that the suspect recently attempted to enter occupied homes. Most residents in the community are over the age of 55.
“One guy was half through a window and the guy inside hit him with a flashlight,” Klwalski said. “As he knew nobody was inside the house, he ended up going out. So they are brave enough to start coming in through windows.”
In response, residents have begun organizing volunteer patrols to help monitor the neighborhood. Police have also increased patrols in the RV park and other similar communities throughout Harlingen.
Officers are encouraging residents to secure their property by locking doors and storage areas, installing surveillance cameras, using light timers, and asking neighbors to watch over homes when they are away.
While no arrests have been made, investigators say they believe a single suspect is responsible for the burglaries.
“From what we’ve seen and are able to tell at this point, we only have the one person,” Harlingen Police Department Sgt. Larry Moore said. “We weren’t able to put any group of people together. We’ve only seen the one person. From all those instances, it’s only been one person that we’ve seen so far.”
Moore said investigators are making progress in the case and remain confident an arrest will be made.
“I wouldn’t say it’s a trend,” Moore said. “Honestly, I think it’s probably one guy, and we’ll find him and it will stop.”
Meanwhile, residents say they plan to continue evening patrols and meet every two weeks to discuss safety concerns and community security efforts.
They also have a message for whoever is responsible.
“Go get a job, don’t rob from us,” Klwalski said. “We seem to be teaming up a little bit more and we are going to be watching,” he added. “So if you are out there doing it, don’t get caught.”
